reforms.description: The federal government has implemented a program that allows small firms to claim R&D credits at a higher rate of 35%, compared to 20% for large firms, to encourage innovation and support growth in the small business sector.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By providing higher R&D credits, the program incentivizes small firms to invest in research and development, which can lead to innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The program allows small firms to claim R&D credits at a higher rate.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform significantly enhances the support for small businesses in R&D, which is crucial for fostering innovation in the economy.
reforms.source_quote: Small firms can claim federal R&D credits at a rate of 35% against only 20% for large firms.

reforms.description: Canada's R&D credit scheme is highlighted as a significant tax subsidy aimed at encouraging private sector research and development, addressing the under-investment in R&D due to externalities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The R&D tax credits are designed to stimulate private investment in research, which can lead to innovation and productivity gains in the economy.
reforms.status_evidence: R&D credits figure among the top 10 federal tax expenditures in Canada.
reforms.importance_rationale: The R&D tax credit scheme represents a structural change in how Canada supports innovation, significantly impacting the private sector's investment in research.
reforms.source_quote: Tax subsidies to private research are used by virtually all OECD countries because of the existence of externalities and therefore under-investment in R&D in the absence of government support.

reforms.description: Canada announced a new science and technology strategy, Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada’s Advantage, which focuses on promoting world-class excellence, prioritizing key areas, encouraging partnerships, and enhancing accountability.
reforms.package_name: Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada’s Advantage
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The strategy aims to enhance Canada's innovation capacity and competitiveness, which can lead to increased productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The new S&T strategy was announced and is being implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in Canada's approach to science and technology, aiming to integrate and prioritize innovation across sectors, which is crucial for long-term economic growth.
reforms.source_quote: In May 2007 Canada announced a new S&T strategy, Mobilising Science and Technology to Canada’s Advantage, which is based on four core principles: promoting world-class excellence, focussing on priorities, encouraging partnerships, and enhancing accountability.

reforms.description: Changes to the phase-out limits for access to the enhanced SR&ED benefits for small businesses were introduced in the 2008 budget, aimed at reducing disincentives to growth.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reducing disincentives for small businesses to grow, this reform encourages investment in R&D, which can lead to innovation and economic expansion.
reforms.status_evidence: Changes to the SR&ED benefits were included in the 2008 budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: This adjustment to the SR&ED benefits is significant for small businesses, as it directly impacts their ability to invest in R&D, thus fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Changes to the phase-out limits for access to the enhanced SR&ED benefits for small businesses in the 2008 budget will reduce the disincentive to growth.

reforms.description: The federal government indicated its willingness to focus funding on priority areas that are in the national interest from a social and economic perspective, including environmental sustainability and energy innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Focusing funding on priority areas can enhance innovation and technological development, leading to improved economic performance and environmental outcomes.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government indicated its willingness to focus funding on priority areas.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in funding priorities, aiming to enhance innovation in key sectors, particularly energy.
reforms.source_quote: In its Science and Technology Strategy, the federal government indicated its willingness to focus funding on priority areas that are in the national interest from a social and economic perspective.

reforms.description: The introduction of a carbon tax in British Columbia aims to internalize the cost of GHG emissions, thereby incentivizing the private sector to invest in sustainable innovations and technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By raising the cost of carbon emissions, the tax encourages firms to innovate and adopt cleaner technologies, potentially leading to long-term economic benefits.
reforms.status_evidence: A more substantial carbon tax has also been introduced in British Columbia and will take effect in July 2008.
reforms.importance_rationale: The carbon tax represents a significant policy tool aimed at reducing emissions and promoting innovation in clean technologies.
reforms.source_quote: A more substantial carbon tax has also been introduced in British Columbia and will take effect in July 2008.

reforms.description: The federal government allocated CAD 240 million to Saskatchewan for a full-scale commercial demonstration of carbon capture and storage technology in the coal-fired electricity sector, aiming to support environmental innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: This initiative aims to develop a technology with significant potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, thereby contributing to environmental sustainability and innovation in the energy sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal Budget provides CAD 240 million in trust for this initiative.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding represents a significant investment in a promising technology that could enhance environmental innovation and sustainability in the energy sector.
reforms.source_quote: The 2008 federal Budget provides CAD 240 million in trust in the fiscal year 2007 to Saskatchewan for this initiative.

reforms.description: The 2007 federal budget established a Major Projects Management Office to streamline the approval process for energy projects, enhancing regulatory efficiency and accountability.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By improving the efficiency of the regulatory process, this initiative is expected to facilitate investment in energy projects, thereby supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: CAD 150 million over five years was allocated to create the Major Projects Management Office.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant step towards improving the regulatory framework for energy projects, which is crucial for attracting investment and fostering innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The 2007 federal budget took an important step in addressing the issue by putting in place a Major Projects Management Office.

reforms.description: The federal government announced the creation of the ecoENERGY for Biofuels Initiative, which will invest up to CAD1.5 billion over nine years to boost Canada’s production of biofuels such as ethanol and biodiesel.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: This initiative aims to enhance the production of renewable energy sources, which can lead to increased innovation in the energy sector and contribute to sustainable economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: On 5 July 2007, the federal government announced the creation of the ecoENERGY for Biofuels Initiative.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant investment in renewable energy, aiming to transform the biofuels sector and promote sustainable energy practices across Canada.
reforms.source_quote: On 5 July 2007, the federal government announced the creation of the ecoENERGY for Biofuels Initiative, which will invest up to CAD1.5 billion over nine years to boost Canada’s production of biofuels such as ethanol and biodiesel.

reforms.description: The government is committed to facilitating the commercialisation of cellulose ethanol, with the 2007 federal Budget allocating CAD500 million for large facilities producing 'next generation' renewables.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By investing in the commercialization of advanced renewable technologies, this initiative is expected to stimulate innovation and economic growth in the renewable energy sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2007 federal Budget allocated CAD500 million for large facilities producing 'next generation' renewables.
reforms.importance_rationale: This funding represents a major commitment to advancing renewable energy technologies, which is crucial for Canada's transition to a sustainable energy future.
reforms.source_quote: The government is committed to facilitating the commercialisation of cellulose ethanol, and the 2007 federal Budget allocated CAD500 million for large facilities producing 'next generation' renewables.

reforms.description: The federal government is encouraging environmental innovation by creating clear and effective policy frameworks, including the Clean Air and Climate Change Trust Fund to support major projects aimed at reducing GHG emissions.
reforms.package_name: Clean Air and Climate Change Initiative
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By establishing frameworks that support environmental innovation, the government aims to foster new technologies and practices that can lead to economic growth and sustainability.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government is encouraging environmental innovation by creating clear and effective policy frameworks.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant shift towards integrating environmental considerations into innovation policy, which is essential for long-term sustainability.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government is encouraging environmental innovation by: i) creating clear and effective policy frameworks for the environment, including the Regulatory Framework for Air Emissions to reduce air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.

reforms.description: The Agriculture Policy Framework (APF) was implemented to reshape Canada's agricultural policies, focusing on long-term viability and competitiveness in the agricultural sector, integrating risk management with innovation and science.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The APF aims to enhance the agricultural sector's growth potential through innovation and improved practices, which can lead to increased productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: The APF was said to be designed to change Canada’s agricultural policy from simply focusing on income support to a more comprehensive approach.
reforms.importance_rationale: The APF represents a structural change in agricultural policy, integrating multiple aspects of agricultural management and innovation, which is crucial for the sector's long-term sustainability and competitiveness.
reforms.source_quote: In essence, the APF was said to be designed to change Canada’s agricultural policy from simply focusing on income support to a more comprehensive approach that would include not only risk management but also the long-run viability of the agriculture and agri-food industry through technology and innovation.

reforms.description: The Canadian government launched an initiative to mandate a 5% ethanol blend in gasoline by 2010 and a 2% biodiesel blend in on-road diesel and heating oil by 2012, alongside budgetary support for production facilities and next-generation technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The initiative aims to reduce reliance on fossil fuels, create new markets for agricultural commodities, and lower greenhouse gas emissions, thereby supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The mandates for ethanol and biodiesel blends were introduced as part of the government's bio-energy production strategy.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant shift in Canada's energy policy, promoting renewable energy sources and aligning agricultural production with environmental goals.
reforms.source_quote: In 2006 the Canadian federal government launched an initiative to mandate a 5% ethanol blend in gasoline by 2010 and a 2% biodiesel blend in on-road diesel and heating oil by 2012.
